page: Combine Middleware for composing multiple middleware functions with logical operators. Three functions provided: some (OR logic, first succeeds stops rest), every (AND logic, all must succeed), except (conditional negation, skip if condition met). Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {some, every, except} from 'hono/combine'. Supports composable patterns for complex access control. Example dependencies: bearerAuth from hono/bearer-auth, getConnInfo from hono/cloudflare-workers, ipRestriction from hono/ip-restriction, rateLimit from custom. Common patterns: some(every(ipRestriction, bearerAuth), rateLimit), some(bearerAuth, rateLimit), every(bearerAuth, rateLimit), except(path, middleware). Applied in order. First successful middleware in some() stops rest. First error in every() stops rest. except() takes string path pattern or function condition, or array for multiple targets. Use cases: skip rate limiting if auth valid, require local network check AND auth, skip auth for public endpoints. Questions: How to combine middleware? What's the difference between some/every/except? How to implement conditional middleware? Can I use complex logic? How do they handle failures? What's the execution order?

sections.manifest: Import statements for Combine middleware functions. import {Hono} from 'hono' for the main framework class. import {some, every, except} from 'hono/combine' for middleware composition functions. Questions: What to import? Where are combination functions? Can I import individual functions?

Combine middleware usage example for complex access control. app.use('*', some(every(ipRestriction(getConnInfo, {allowList: ['192.168.0.2']}), bearerAuth({token})), rateLimit())). Pattern: some(AND condition, fallback). If ipRestriction AND bearerAuth both succeed, rateLimit skipped. Otherwise, rateLimit applies. Uses getConnInfo from hono/cloudflare-workers for IP information. allowList parameter for ipRestriction with array of allowed IPs. Responds with c.text('Hello Hono!'). Questions: How to combine conditions? How to implement OR logic? How to implement AND logic? Can I use getConnInfo? What about IP restrictions? Does order matter?

some() function: OR logic, run first succeeding middleware. Runs given middleware in order. First to complete successfully stops subsequent ones. Example: some(bearerAuth({token}), myRateLimit({limit: 100})). Semantics: if bearer auth succeeds, skip rate limit; otherwise, apply rate limit. Practical: skip rate limiting for authenticated users. Execution stops on first success. Questions: How does some() work? What if none succeed? How to implement optional middleware? What's the execution order?

every() function: AND logic, run all middleware, fail on first error. Runs given middleware in order. All must succeed; first error stops rest. Example: every(bearerAuth({token}), myRateLimit({limit: 100})). Execution: must pass both auth AND rate limit checks. Practical: require multiple conditions like local network check AND auth. Fails when any middleware throws. Questions: How does every() work? Do all have to succeed? What if one fails? How to implement mandatory conditions?

except() function: conditional negation, skip middleware if condition met. Condition types: string (path pattern like '/api/public/*'), function ((c: Context) => boolean). Multiple targets: pass array. Example: except('/api/public/*', bearerAuth({token})). Semantics: skip auth for /api/public/*, require auth for others. Practical: public endpoints bypass authentication. Condition evaluated per request. Questions: How does except() work? What condition formats supported? How to match multiple paths? Can I use functions? What about complex conditions?
